analysis.one_liner: Grasim is an Aditya Birla Group conglomerate whose own business is viscose fibre and chemicals, but most of its market value sits in its controlling stakes in UltraTech Cement and Aditya Birla Capital, plus newer paints and B2B e-commerce ventures.
analysis.whats_happening: Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 2026) results, released 12 August 2026, showed consolidated revenue of ₹48,716 crore (up 21% YoY) and EBITDA of ₹8,077 crore (up 26% YoY, management called it the highest-ever quarterly EBITDA). Adjusted PAT was ₹2,153 crore, up 49% YoY, though the prior-year base was restated for an insurance accounting standard change (Ind AS 117), so that YoY jump isn't a clean like-for-like comparison. Q2 FY27 results are expected around 14 November 2026 (a single source cited this date; treat it as likely but not fully confirmed via exchange filing) — about four weeks away, not imminent.
analysis.plain_terms: Think of Grasim less as a single company and more as the holding vehicle for a chunk of the Aditya Birla Group's empire: its own fibre and chemicals business is sizeable but modest, while a large part of its value comes from stakes in UltraTech Cement and Aditya Birla Capital. The tension is that newer bets — Birla Opus paints and a B2B e-commerce arm — are growing revenue very fast (paints up 64% YoY, e-commerce up 75% YoY) but neither is profitable yet, and management itself says paints won't likely break even until it reaches ₹10,000 crore in revenue, a target pegged to FY28. That drags down overall return ratios even as the topline growth story looks exciting.
analysis.quarters: Across Q1 FY27, every reported segment grew revenue: cellulosic fibres +12% YoY (export volumes more than doubled even as domestic volume fell 4%), chemicals +10% YoY with EBITDA up a faster 16%, cement (UltraTech) +16% YoY on 12.2% higher volumes, paints +64% YoY (off a small base, so the percentage overstates scale), and B2B e-commerce +75% YoY (also off a small base). Standalone EBITDA more than doubled YoY (+107%) on cellulosic fibres and chemicals strength. Management flagged that consolidated PAT growth (+49% YoY) benefited from a restated prior-year base due to an insurance accounting standard change at Aditya Birla Capital — so that figure is not strictly comparable and should be read with that caveat rather than taken at face value.
analysis.performance_read: Over 5 years the stock has returned 70.91% versus the Nifty's 25.27% and peer UltraTech's 53.84% — a clear outperformance. Over the last year it is roughly flat (+2.42%) while both the Nifty (-9.53%) and the peer (-9.94%) fell, so it has held up well in a weak market rather than rallying. The only corporate action on record is a 5:1 split from October 2016, well before this performance window, so none of these returns need adjustment for spin-offs or demergers. The stock is currently 13.6% below its August 2026 peak of ₹3,380.5 — a pullback within a longer uptrend, not evidence of a structural problem. With a dividend yield of just 0.34%, nearly all of the return here comes from price appreciation, not income.
analysis.valuation_read: P/E estimates from different sources range from about 34x to 38x, and ROE is low at roughly 5% (one source showed a conflicting 10.32% figure that could not be reconciled, so treat the lower figure as more reliable pending verification). Why it looks expensive: a meaningful share of consolidated capital is tied up in paints and B2B e-commerce, businesses that are pre-profitability, which drags down blended return ratios even though the core fibre, chemicals and cement businesses are performing well. Whether it is actually cheap or expensive is a different question — sum-of-the-parts analysis from Morgan Stanley attributes roughly 68% of Grasim's value to its UltraTech stake alone, which argues the standalone P/E is the wrong lens; investors weighing this stock are really betting on when the newer businesses turn profitable, not on the current blended multiple.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is broad-based rather than coming from one lever: cement is largely volume-led (+12.2% tonnes), chemicals is more margin-led (EBITDA growing faster than revenue), and paints/e-commerce are early-stage businesses scaling off a small base where high percentage growth reflects the small denominator rather than market dominance. Overall this is a growing business, but the quality of that growth varies sharply by segment — mature segments (fibre, chemicals, cement) are growing profitably while the newest ones are still growing their way toward profitability.
analysis.health_read: Standalone net debt rose from ₹7,327 crore (March 2026) to ₹9,899 crore (June 2026); the company attributes this to a timing mismatch — it funded an investment into Aditya Birla Capital before receiving its UltraTech dividend. Consolidated net debt/EBITDA improved sharply to 1.45x (June 2026) from 4.6x (March 2026). Note that total consolidated borrowings of roughly ₹2.27 lakh crore mostly reflect Aditya Birla Capital's lending book, not core industrial debt, so it shouldn't be read as leverage risk on the manufacturing business. Credit ratings (AAA/Stable from CRISIL and ICRA, reaffirmed May-June 2026) suggest financial risk is well contained; the real open question is business risk — whether paints and e-commerce convert their revenue growth into profit on the timelines management has set out.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding (Birla family via Birla Group Holdings, IGH Holdings, Pilani Investment, Hindalco and others) stood at 43.74% as of the June 2026 quarterly filing. A later disclosure (September 2026) indicated cumulative open-market buying had taken this toward 45.07%, though that figure comes from an informal disclosure of buying activity since February 2024 rather than a confirmed quarterly shareholding filing — the official September-quarter pattern isn't published yet. Multiple sources confirm zero promoter pledging. No marquee or celebrity individual investor appears on the shareholder register; the non-promoter base is dominated by FIIs (~17%) and DIIs (~16%), not a known name.
strengths: Consolidated EBITDA of ₹8,077 crore in Q1 FY27, described by management as the highest-ever quarter, up 26% YoY
Cement volumes (via UltraTech) up 12.2% YoY to 41.3 million tonnes, with capacity expansion underway to 240+ MTPA by March 2028
Zero promoter pledging, with promoters net buyers taking their stake from ~43% toward ~45%
Consolidated net debt/EBITDA improved to 1.45x (June 2026) from 4.6x (March 2026), with AAA/Stable ratings reaffirmed
watchpoints: ROE of only about 5% despite a P/E in the mid-30s, meaning the stock is priced ahead of its blended profitability today
Birla Opus paints not expected to be profitable until it crosses ₹10,000 crore in revenue, a target management ties to FY28 — a multi-year wait
Standalone net debt rose roughly 35% in a single quarter (₹7,327 crore to ₹9,899 crore); management calls it a timing issue but it's worth watching next quarter
Stock is 13.6% off its August 2026 peak and the dividend yield is only 0.34%, so near-term returns depend almost entirely on continued price appreciation
analysis.one_thing: Watch Birla Opus paints' and Birla Pivot e-commerce's revenue trajectory against management's own profitability targets (paints breakeven tied to ₹10,000 crore revenue around FY28; e-commerce EBITDA breakeven targeted by exit of FY27) — that will determine whether Grasim's currently weak ~5% ROE starts to improve.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 revenue, EBITDA and segment figures are cross-checked across the company's own press release (grasim.com), Aditya Birla Group's release, and independent coverage (Business Standard, Zeebiz, Investing.com) and are reasonably consistent. However, ROE (4.98% vs a conflicting 10.32% from another source), ROCE (8.01% vs internally inconsistent figures elsewhere), P/E (34.4 vs 38.3 across sources) and one brokerage's target price (₹3,600 vs ₹3,800) could not be reconciled and should be checked directly on Screener before use. The Q2 FY27 results date (14 November 2026) comes from a single source and is not independently confirmed via an exchange filing. A reported Canadian pulp-JV mill idling (September 2026) came from only one outlet and is unverified by a second source.
